title: 2026 World Series: Well-rested Brewers come back fresh thanks to all the winning - CBS Sports
description: MILWAUKEE -- The Milwaukee Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series, 3-2, Friday night at American Family Field. It was their first win si
body:
MILWAUKEE -- The Milwaukee Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series, 3-2, Friday night at American Family Field. It was their first win since Thursday, Oct. 15. They hadn't lost since then either, though; they had been off. Any time a team has a long layoff in the postseason, we end up hearing the same tired song and dance. "Rust vs. Rest" is the succinct headline. The basic argument is that with baseball being a daily sport in the regular season, teams sitting around for multiple days between series -- or between the end of the regular season and the divisional series -- are at some sort of disadvantage because they'll come out rusty. It's nonsense, of course. One example obviously doesn't disprove a theory -- though we have several more and we'll get to those -- but the Brewers are doing their best to kill that narrative.In the first inning of World Series Game 1 on Friday, Jackson Chourio led off with a single. Christian Yelich tripled him home and then scored on a William Contreras single. In the span of four batters, the team that spent seven full days without playing a game just scored two runs. Nick Martinez, on the mound for the Rays, wasn't great in the second half, but he was an All-Star this season and was coming off an outing in which he allowed only one run in more than five innings against the Guardians in the ALCS.
Was Contreras rusty? After that RBI single in the first, he threw out two runners trying to steal and nailed both of his ABS challenges. It sure seems like a rusty catcher wouldn't be so excellent behind the plate at judging balls and strikes. "Contreras was unbelievable," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after the game. "The two caught stealings, the ABS, the hits, calling the game." ... Now, we did not play great. You can look back and we made a baserunning mistake, we made an execution mistake. We made a defensive mistake. We weren't perfect. But after being off for some time, I'm pleased we came out in the first inning ready to go."
The wait between sweeping the Dodgers in the NLDS and Game 1 of the World Series wasn't the Brewers' only break. They have now played just nine games in 26 days. They've won eight of them. It sort of blows up that "rusty" argument, doesn't it?As all teams with long layoffs do, the Brewers had plenty of practices. These days, that's not just swings off batting practice pitchers; Trajekt technology uses holograms of real pitchers and recreates everything about their pitches, including spin rate, velocity, movement, the works. The tech has gotten so good that players have started bypassing minor-league rehab assignments after injury absences and instead just getting back up to game speed using the Trajekt machines.The Brewers also played practice games. "We played baseball, that's how we prepared," Murphy said on Thursday before their team workout. "We went out there and played baseball every day, live at-bats. You can't recreate real, you know what I mean? It's a long layoff, and if we want to use it as an excuse, then let people use it as an excuse, but I refuse to do that."
I'm glad he said something about excuses, because some of the narratives we've seen used with teams after layoffs in the past are tantamount to excuse-making. When high-seeded teams lose a game or even a series, people love to cling to excuses instead of just accepting that baseball in small samples lends itself to variance. Sure, we've heard former players making claims like your body doesn't adjust well to not playing games for multiple days after having played nearly every day for six months, and maybe they do feel that, but the numbers tell us otherwise.The 2022 and 2023 Braves seemed to be the poster child for this under the current playoff format, which debuted in 2022. How many times did we hear about how unfair it was that the top two seeds were forced to sit around and get rusty while the lower seeds get to play meaningful baseball, giving them a supposed edge?
Rubbish. Utter rubbish. That very argument ignored the top-seeded Astros in 2022. They got a bye and then swept the Mariners in the ALDS, waited a few more days off and then swept the Yankees in the ALCS. They had another long layoff before the World Series and then beat the Phillies six games. They went 11-2 in all, the best record in this iteration of the playoffs. If the Brewers sweep here, they'll beat it.In the current playoff format, teams with at least five days of rest before Game 1 have gone 14-10 in Games 1. You might think 10 losses is too many, but that record is a 162-game pace of 95 wins, and these are obviously all games against playoff teams. The rested teams are good, not rusty. Let's get back to the Brewers. They earned the spotlight just as they've been doing all playoffs and, really, nearly the entire season. They earned the rest during their bye by having the best record in baseball with 103 wins. They earned their days off before the NLCS by getting rid of the Padres in four games instead of five. They earned more than a week of rest before the World Series by taking out the two-time defending champion Dodgers in a four-game sweep. 
We already discussed the offense and Contreras behind the plate, but the Brewers again played great defense overall. There was one misplay in center in the fourth inning, but it was on a hard line drive right at Garrett Mitchell and those are always difficult to judge. The scorekeeper ruled it a double anyway, not an error.Jacob Misiorowski, who has now thrown more than 40 innings over his previous career-high workload, saw his velocity tick up over his season average. He hadn't pitched since Oct. 11 and got deeper into the game than his previous two playoff starts. The Brewers are a team that shortens games with their bullpen, and while they have depth, they'd prefer to ride their three back-inning beasts in Abner Uribe, Aaron Ashby and Trevor Megill. With all that rest, that trio has been able to impact nearly every game. Those three combined for four innings of work to close down Game 1 and they'll likely all be available for a similar workload in Game 2. In fact, even if they combine for four innings again in Game 2, there's a day off before Game 3, so it wouldn't be surprising to see this exact formula for each of the first three games. Hell, they could do it in Game 4, too. 
Murphy himself said the rest was good for his squad. "We needed a little bit of a break," he said on Thursday. "It was an emotional series in L.A. Cross-country trip, all that. We had a few days where it was a little lighter, but then we've picked it up and gotten a lot of live ABs, but nothing simulates the game the way it is."The rest is what is setting the Brewers up for what could well be a historic run. Again, they've only played nine games in the last 26 days, but that is because they played such great baseball that they earned their rest. Winning means rest, and rest means winning.In order for the Rays to win the World Series, they'll now have to beat the Brewers four times in the next five or six games. To find the Brewers' last four losses, we'd have to go back to Sept. 13. They've gone 18-3 since then, despite having all those days off. 
They didn't forget how to play baseball. They may just have forgotten how to lose.

title: Cowboys' George Pickens deflects Brian Schottenheimer's critique, says team needs to improve - CBS Sports
description: FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (2-4) are in a rut offensively.After their last two primetime losses against the Tampa Bay Buccaneer
body:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (2-4) are in a rut offensively.After their last two primetime losses against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (24-16) and the Green Bay Packers (23-13) in Weeks 5 and 6, the Cowboys have now scored fewer than 20 points in consecutive Dak Prescott starts for the first time since 2019, Jason Garrett's last year as the team's head coach. One of the issues plaguing current Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer's offense is Dallas' 31st-ranked rushing offense (76.0 rushing yards per game). The Cowboys have run the football on a league-low 32.5% of their plays, and on Thursday, Schottenheimer criticized Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens for his effort as run blocker and how hard he runs when Dallas is trying to run the ball. Dallas' head coach and offensive play-caller feels it is harder to succeed in selling the run to set up play-action passes, with Pickens showing what Schottenheimer perceives as effort that needs improvement on run plays.After practice on Friday, Pickens chose to deflect from directly addressing his head coach's comments and to focus on what the entire Cowboys offense needs to do to fix their lagging run game. His 1,429 receiving yards in 2025 ranked third in the NFL, and his 428 this season sit outside of the top 10 at No. 12 in the league."I feel like, like I said, as a team, I feel like run, pass, a lot of stuff, you know what I mean? One week, it was you guys [the media] were saying defense [needs improvement]; one week you're saying this," Pickens said. "I feel like if you narrow the comments down, you're talking about the team. So most definitely, I feel like as a team, just keep improving."   
Since the Cowboys acquired Pickens in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers in May of 2025, he and fellow Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb have become fast friends. Lamb hasn't seen any dip from Pickens despite comments made by people inside or outside the Cowboys' facility about Dallas' explosive wideout."I don't think about it [the criticism]. I hang around GP more than pretty much anyone in this building, and I'm always going to be on his side. To answer your question [Lamb shrugged, tilted his head and gave a wry grin]. We're cool man," Lamb said Friday. "He [Pickens] comes in ready to work every opportunity. It doesn't seem to bother him. It's not like we sit around and talk about the bad things people say. As far as his approach, coming to work and being the same guy every single day, he still does it."  Why the Cowboys offense needs to be focused on balance to see explosive plays returnGenerating explosive plays in both the run and pass games could also help bring the run game back to life. The Cowboys' 34 explosive plays, which TruMedia defines as catches of 16 or more yards and runs of 12 or more yards, rank 22nd in the NFL entering Week 7. Last season, Dallas had 127 explosive plays, the seventh most in the NFL. Just over 73% of those explosives in 2025 were on pass plays (93), with Pickens accounting for over a third of those explosive catches with 34 in 2025, the fourth most in the NFL. Entering Week 7 this season, Pickens' 10 explosive receptions rank 17th in the league. 
So what does Pickens need to do to get involved early in games? In his mind, he's already doing it. "I'm doing what they're telling me to do," Pickens said. "So, [keep] doing what they tell me to do."  He also feels that having a more balanced offense could help create the explosives and the big plays to himself and others. The 25-year-old mentioned how, when playing college football video games, some teams will have their offenses listed as "Air Raid" or "Ground and Pound." Pickens' preferred offense would be one that is labeled "balanced." He also disputed the need to have the ball in his hands right away on game day to get in the flow of the action. 
"I wouldn't really say that because ... [if] you can run the ball, [if] you can pass it, it's more about balance. It's not really about me or anyone else," Pickens said. "As a team, how would you run your offense or how you run your defense even if you're playing a video game?"Execution, just making plays plain and simple, could also be a quick fix. The Cowboys have been blitzed more often as of late, and they haven't been able to set up quarterback Dak Prescott to succeed nearly as well on those plays when it comes to blocking and being on the same page when the pressure comes. In 2025, Prescott's passer rating when blitzed was 103.8. This year, it's down to 89.1."Execute properly. We leave explosives out there on the field just about every week. I hate to say that, but you look at it on film, and it's all over the tape," Lamb said. "Just being able to execute and being on the same page with sight adjustments. We feel like everybody else feels like if they blitz us, they're going to have a better chance of winning the game. I don't believe that, but they've [opponents] been having a lot of success at doing that. Being on the same page and executing properly."
Cowboys offensive tendencies under Brian Schottenheimer, Since 2025 (NFL ranks)20252026Motion rate56.6% (13th)42.7% (31st)Play action rate28.2% (9th)24.2% (20th)Under center rate38.4% (11th)30.4% (28th)Shotgun rate61.6% (22nd)69.6% (5th)Run rate41.5% (24th)32.5% (Last)Tempo (average time between snaps in seconds)32.9 (Fastest)33.4 (Fastest)The Pickens effectHaving the explosives back in the Cowboys' offense could help Dallas rediscover the spark and offensive rhythm it had in Year 1 under Schottenheimer last season. Pickens getting the football is a big part of that. "I think it would help my teammates tremendously. As far as me, Javonte [Williams], Turp [KaVontae Turpin], Flo [Ryan Flournoy], Cee [CeeDee Lamb], Ferg [Jake Ferguson], anybody we can get going early, I feel like we'll spark off of it. That's why I'm saying more balance, you know what I mean?"Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams agreed, saying he can feel the edge and excitement when Pickens makes a big play and begins to trash talk the defense despite being all the way up in the coach's box on game day. "I think the intention has certainly been there. It's been part of the discussion when you're putting together plays early," Adams said on Friday. "One of the things that we started seeing at the end of last season is that we're seeing a little bit, or a lot a bit, we're getting played differently than what we're seeing on tape. So there have been games this year where the first quarter has been like 'alright, that's not what we were planning on seeing, we need to get to X,Y,Z.' Sometimes a lot of coaching on game day gets you out of your planned openers, or there are times where he is drawing a double early, and putting him and CeeDee on the same side where you're going to get three coverage pieces, sometimes it's difficult to get him the ball in those scenarios.""The best way to answer that is I have to do a better job of making sure he gets it [the ball] because he is a bright spot for us when he has the ball in his hands," Adams continued. "And for a lack of a better term, talking shit to the defense. I know that I get excited."Prescott called Pickens' edge "infectious" and something that gives the Cowboys key momentum. "We just have to get him the ball early, I definitely think that would help," Prescott said Friday. ... "He's a guy who is infectious to the team when he catches the ball. Whether it be a celebration or run after catch, it's good momentum we can build off of."  So how can Dallas scheme up early looks to Pickens? One option is putting him and Lamb on the same side of the formation, and then freeing Pickens up off a route that pulls him away from the gravity Lamb draws. Another way would be getting him the football early underneath on a screen, something Adams acknowledged as a legitimate option. "If you know you're going to put those two guys [Lamb and Pickens] on the same side and get a certain coverage, that's a way to do it," Adams said. "Guys like CeeDee, we sometimes give him the sweep [run play], that's an easy way to do it. I think just kind of brainstorming through the easiest vision that you can get a guy is sometimes the best one. Sometimes if you think you can ensure they're not getting coverage over the top, those guys like when you throw the fade ball toward them."Regardless, the Cowboys need to rediscover how to maximize all the playmaking talent they have on offense ASAP, starting with their "Monday Night Football" matchup at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) with the NFC East up for grabs. This season's NFC East became the first division ever to go winless in consecutive weeks with a combined 0-6-2 record since Week 5, but the Cowboys know their chance to capitalize on their rivals' slip ups is now or never. "I would say determined, and I hope urgent. We can only say, 'We've got a lot of games in front of us' for so long," Prescott said of the Cowboys' mindset. "Might be already past us, right?  We've got to go win. You want to give yourself a chance to be a winning team, to be a playoff team, you got to win as many games as you can. And when you drop two games, and particularly games that we didn't expect to drop, it makes it that much harder. So, urgent. Urgent to get it done now."

title: Robbie Avila cleared to return to Saint Louis: Judge rules Billikens star can be added to roster - CBS Sports
description: A judge granted a temporary restraing order Friday  for Avila to play just days before the season begins
body:
A judge granted a temporary restraing order Friday  for Avila to play just days before the season begins
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Saint Louis star Robbie Avila could be returning to the Billikens after a judge granted a temporary restraining order Friday allowing him another season of eligibility, according to media reports.The judge, Jason Sengheiser, ruled that Avila, who was seeking a fifth year of eligibility in the courts and is already enrolled at Saint Louis for this school year, can be placed on Saint Louis' roster for the 2026-27 season.Saint Louis opens the season Nov. 2 vs. Lehigh before Avila is scheduled to appear in court on Nov. 4 for a another hearing.Avila has become one of the most polarizing and entertaining players in college basketball to watch, dating back to his time at Indiana State. Avila helped Indiana State reach the NIT title game in 2024 before following his coach, Josh Schertz, to Saint Louis that offseason.
Avila averaged 12.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.1 assists during the 2025-26 season at Saint Louis and led his team to the second round of the NCAA Tournament before the Billikens lost to eventual national champion Michigan. With Avila eligible to play (for now), Saint Louis is set to return 10 players -- including six of its seven top scorers -- from a team that won 29 games.After going undrafted in the 2026 NBA Draft, Avila signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Los Angeles Lakers and played with the franchise in summer league. An Exhibit 10 contract is a one-year, non-guaranteed contract that allows players to compete for a roster spot in training camp.
Although the ACC, Big 12, Big Ten and SEC have been among the conferences to speak out and set sidelines about professional athletes returning to college, the Atlantic 10 has yet to set forth any guidelines surrounding the topic.

title: 2026 World Series: Brandon Woodruff makes Brewers' roster after long injury layoff - CBS Sports
description: Woodruff, who debuted with Milwaukee in 2017, hasn't pitched since July 4 due to a shoulder issue
body:
Woodruff, who debuted with Milwaukee in 2017, hasn't pitched since July 4 due to a shoulder issue
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Right-hander Brandon Woodruff, the longest-tenured player on the Milwaukee Brewers, has made the club's World Series roster. Woodruff has not pitched in an MLB game since July 4 due to what was initially considered a severe shoulder injury, though he showed enough improvement in August to begin a throwing program. Game 1 of the Fall Classic between the Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays is set for Friday night in Milwaukee. "We know who the kid is. We know his -- that it's not going to be too much for him. This is what this kid's all about. He's been around here for ten years or whatever, and we've understood it. We feel like there's a window where he can help us," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said on Friday."That was the whole decision. This isn't a, 'wow, we love Woody, he's great for the organization' -- because he already said to us, I don't want to be a sympathy pick. I want to be a pick because I can help the team. Then you go through all the things and say, can he help us? The answer is yes, he can definitely help us."
        
            
                Three biggest questions for World Series Game 1 as Brewers and Rays kick off 2026 Fall Classic
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Now 33, Woodruff made nine effective starts prior to the shoulder injury this season. He missed the entire 2024 season after having surgery on his shoulder, returned to make 12 starts in 2025, and then was on the Opening Day roster this year. It was initially feared that Woodruff would require another surgery in July. That ultimately was not the case.
Murphy acknowledged the roster rules would play a role in carrying Woodruff on the World Series roster. Injured players can be replaced on the postseason roster if they suffer a new injury. By rule, the Brewers would not be able to replace Woodruff if he suffers a setback and re-injures his shoulder. They're gambling that his shoulder will hold up.
"I didn't want this to be a charity pick," Woodruff said on Friday. "That was important to me. I wanted to feel like I could -- I wanted to be on the roster because I felt like I could help win. So I did not want this to be part of the decision."Woodruff said he met with Murphy and president of baseball operations Matt Arnold on Thursday before the final decision was made.
"It didn't really hit me," he said of the call from Murphy to tell him he'd made the roster. "I was kind of like thank you for the opportunity and, basically, let's go win this thing. That was pretty much the extent of the conversation. It was like they've got work to do, I've got a job to do to mentally prepare, and I just thanked them. That was pretty much it, yeah."During his nine starts this season, Woodruff pitched to a 2.98 ERA with 47 strikeouts and only nine unintentional walks in 45 ⅓ innings. At times, his fastball clocked as high as 96.0 mph. There were also times when he sat in the upper 80s. The movement traits on his fastball remain terrific, allowing it to play at reduced velocity.It is unknown how the Brewers intend to use Woodruff, though it seems likely he won't be much more than a one- or two-inning option given the injury and long layoff. Truth be told, he may only see the mound in a blowout. Regardless, the Brewers consider him healthy enough to contribute in some capacity. Woodruff, who has spent his entire MLB career with the Brewers after debuting in 2017, replaced right-hander Chad Patrick on the roster. Patrick was on the NLDS and NLCS rosters, but did not pitch.
Game 1 of the World Series will be played Friday night at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Both the Brewers and Rays are seeking their first-ever championship. National League Cy Young favorite Jacob Misiorowski will start for the Brewers, while the Rays counter with Nick Martinez -- a somewhat unexpected choice.

title: Mavericks star Cooper Flagg injured on flagrant foul by Pacers' Aaron Nesmith - CBS Sports
description: The reigning NBA Rookie of the Year hurt his shoulder, and the Mavericks got into with Nesmith on Friday night
body:
The reigning NBA Rookie of the Year hurt his shoulder, and the Mavericks got into with Nesmith on Friday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Cooper Flagg, the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year, left the Dallas Mavericks' 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday with a left shoulder injury just before halftime after being on the receiving end of a flagrant foul by Aaron Nesmith. Mavericks coach Dusty May said that Flagg was in "good spirits" in the locker room, but will be evaluated in the "next couple of days." The Mavericks are set to host the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday before going back on the road to face the Miami Heat on Monday. It's unclear if Flagg will play in either of those games. With a minute to play in the first half in Indianapolis, Flagg got a steal and took off the other way on a fast break. It seemed he would have an easy dunk until Nesmith raced in from behind and sent him sprawling with a hard foul. Flagg immediately grabbed for his shoulder, while Mavericks forward Naji Marshall confronted Nesmith under the basket, which led to a big scrum involving players from both teams. Here's a look at the play:
After a review, the foul was upgraded to a Flagrant 1 on Nesmith, and Marshall and Nesmith both received technicals. Flagg made both of his free throws before leaving the game for good. 
"Nesmith's a great guy. Heck of a player. I've known him since he was in high school. An unfortunate play. Hopefully Coop's fine, but obviously it's something we wish wouldn't have happened," May said. 
After putting up 24 points in the win, Kyrie Irving explained why the Mavericks were so quick to stand up for Flagg. "We've got to set an example for every single one of us, especially Coop, our youngest guy on the team. We gotta protect him, and when we see him go down like that, it doesn't make us feel good," Irving said. "That's NBA basketball, it's a brotherhood you create within that locker room. You can see the difference when teams don't show up for each other and we don't want to be one of those teams, so when anyone goes down, especially Coop or myself or anybody, we gotta have each other's back, and we're a family out here and that's the atmosphere we gotta create."Flagg averaged 21 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals last season, and was off to a stellar start in his sophomore campaign. He poured in 32 points on 10 of 17 from the field in the Mavericks' season-opening loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday and had 14 points, five rebounds, six assists and three steals on 4 of 6 shooting in 17 minutes on Friday before he was injured. 
After his stellar rookie season, Flagg checked in at No. 25 on CBS Sports' Top 100 NBA players ranking, which was released earlier this month.

title: Fever's Krauskopf steps down, Cox fired: What it means for Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell - CBS Sports
description: Indiana is making sweeping changes as it tries to build a championship team around Caitlin Clark, whose co-star,
body:
Indiana is making sweeping changes as it tries to build a championship team around Caitlin Clark, whose co-star, Kelsey Mitchell, is an unrestricted free agent
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Indiana Fever are undergoing a major front-office shakeup. President of basketball and business operations Kelly Krauskopf has stepped down and general manager Amber Cox has been fired. The team announced Krauskopf's decision to step away on Friday morning before later announcing Cox's departure. Krauskopf was the Fever's original president and general manager for their inaugural season in 2000, and remained in that role until 2018, when the Indiana Pacers hired her as their assistant general manager and she became the first woman in NBA history to hold an executive basketball management role. During her first stint with the Fever, Krauskopf built one of the most consistent organizations in the league. The Fever made the playoffs 13 times in her 19 seasons, including 12 consecutive seasons from 2005-16, which remains a WNBA record. Under Krauskopf's leadership, the Fever won their first and only title in 2012, and also reached the Finals in 2009 and 2015. 
        
            
                What's next for Fever? After playoff exit, Indiana must determine if Caitlin Clark-Kelsey Mitchell duo can win
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Krauskopf returned to the Fever in 2024 and was part of the organization's decision to hire Cox as chief operating officer and general manager. That was the same year Caitlin Clark arrived and the franchise's worldwide popularity exploded. The Fever made the playoffs in each of the last three seasons, but never advanced past the semifinals, and Krauskopf and Cox have both faced criticism for failing to build a better team around Clark, Aliyah Boston, and Kelsey Mitchell. The organizational shakeup comes as an important offseason for the franchise is underway. Mitchell is an unrestricted free agent, but now the Fever are without a president and general manager. Krauskopf informed the organization of her decision prior to the end of the season, so you'd assume the organization has been working on a succession plan, but the Fever will need to make some decisions quickly. 
This is a critical offseason for the franchise, and whoever replaces Krauskopf and Cox will immediately be thrown into the fire.Why is this such an important offseason for the Fever?After a first-round exit to the Las Vegas Aces, the Fever have some major items on the agenda this offseason. First and foremost, they want to re-sign Mitchell, who is an unrestricted free agent. Cox said Mitchell will be a "major priority," and it's fair to assume the new front office will feel the same way. Clark, for her part, said that she and her teammates will recruit Mitchell "as hard as we can." Mitchell, however, is unsure of her future with the Fever, who drafted her No. 2 overall back in 2018.
"I have to be selfish," Mitchell said during her exit interview. "I think that's where I am in my career ... what I probably need and what's probably best for me. So I have to be selfish in that room. "But I think, ultimately, being on the Fever and being a part of an organization that does come with a lot of ups and downs, what factors in and what is important for me is, obviously, having a good chemistry on and off the floor. I've only been with one team my entire career, so it's all kind of like figuring this out. It's hard, man."
        
            
                Kelsey Mitchell landing spots: Three title contenders that make sense if WNBA scoring champion leaves Fever
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Clark, meanwhile, is eligible for an EPIC (Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract) extension, which allows players to renegotiate the fourth year of their rookie contract and sign a three-year extension. During her exit interview, Clark hinted at being willing to take a discount, but did not say whether she'll sign an EPIC deal."I think for myself, my focus is on winning. I certainly know what I deserve and what I'm worth, but at the same time, sometimes you have to make sacrifices," Clark said. 
The Mitchell and Clark contract decisions will complicate an already messy cap sheet for the Fever. Even if both were willing to take a slight discount to return, the Fever would still have three players -- including Boston, who signed an EPIC extension last offseason -- taking up about 60% of the salary cap moving forward, and it's not easy to build a championship roster with so few resources for everyone else. That's especially true when the Fever still have Monique Billings and Lexie Hull on the books for $800K apiece next season -- the result of a pair of disastrous deals Krauskopf and Cox handed out last offseason. Stephanie White expected to remain as coachAhead of the 2025 season, Krauskopf and Cox fired coach Christie Sides and replaced her with the veteran Stephanie White, who played for the Fever from 2000-04 and previously served as an assistant coach from 2011-14 and head coach from 2015-16. White has one year remaining on her contract and is expected to remain in her role, according to The Athletic. White has made the playoffs in each of her two seasons in charge, and the Fever's 24 wins this season were a franchise record. However, the team has not advanced past the semifinals, and White has faced steady criticism for how she's handled Clark and the team overall. 
Clark has routinely backed White, though, and did so again at her exit interview. "I really appreciate Steph. I like to say this is the best job in women's basketball and possibly women's sports, getting to lead this franchise that has so much notoriety, but at the same time, it can come with some negatives and people are gonna criticize everything that you can do. That's just the reality, people expect greatness," Clark said. "Personally, my relationship with Steph, she's somebody that's always supported me. It's been really fun getting to play for her," Clark continued. "She just tries to win, she's competitive. She expects great things out of us. She has a fiery passion about her that I really, really admire. I think I have a lot of that in myself too. One of my most special memories of this year is getting to win a gold medal with her in Berlin. That's not something anybody can ever take away from us." 
New front office has work to do to repair reputationDuring Game 2 of the Fever's first-round series with the Aces, MVP A'ja Wilson confronted a fan sitting along the baseline, who she felt had been disrespectful. Wilson received a technical foul for the incident, which became a national talking point and reignited the discourse about Fever fans and the organization's reputation. During her exit interview, Cox said that "attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality, and they need to stop. "Every organization in the league, every organization throughout professional sports, all the way down to youth rec leagues, have to deal with occasional bad behavior from spectators. And anyone who crosses the line in an arena or online needs to be held accountable. I want to be really clear about that. There is a line, and people need to be held accountable if they cross it," Cox said. 
"But here's the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season. Not one fan was removed from a game. ... Our fans love this team. They're going to cheer, they're going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It's a home-court advantage for a reason, and it's the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct."That same day, however, Mitchell admitted that she didn't always enjoy playing in front of Fever fans. "Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard," Mitchell said. "I think this organization is unbelievable, man, but I think that when it comes to, like, really trying to be yourself, it hasn't always been easy."
Early on Friday, prior to the changes in the Fever's front office, The Athletic published a report in which one agent said that multiple of their clients had been called the N-word in Indianapolis. And earlier this season, Alyssa Thomas and DeWanna Bonner said they received death threats and had their addresses leaked after Thomas was retroactively assessed a Flagrant 2 foul and suspended for one game following an in-game altercation with Clark. During her exit interview, Clark once again denounced fans who use her name for the wrong reasons. "As far as people that have used me to demonstrate racist rhetoric or hate or discrimination, that's not something I stand for," Clark said. "That's never been something I've stood for. For those of you that know me, that's not what I'm about, that's not how I was raised, so that's really disappointing when people do that."In addition to recruiting Mitchell and figuring out Clark's extension, the Fever's new front office will have to repair the franchise's reputation around the league.

        The Baltimore Ravens could be on the verge of getting their starting quarterback back in the lineup. Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last two-and-a-half games due to an ankle injury, said on Friday that he is hopeful to play on Sunday against the division rival Cincinnati Bengals."Right now, I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said. "I can't call it right now. I've still got a little grace period. So, we'll see man. Hopefully, but I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now."Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson got a "pretty good amount of work in" during Friday's practice after he was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, but stated that the team is "still working through" whether or not Jackson will play on Sunday.For his part, Jackson said the Ravens' medical staff told him he is dealing with a high ankle sprain, per The Athletic, which he seemingly sustained on the final play of the first half of the Ravens' victory over the Tennessee Titans back in Week 4. Jackson has been described as "day-to-day" since the injury, but this week was the first time he has participated in practice since going down.
He said on Friday that he doesn't have to be 100% healthy to play, but he doesn't want to be a "statue" on the field, via The Athletic. Jackson also relayed that the decision to play through multiple injuries that limited his mobility last season was "dumb, a little bit."Jackson's rushing ability was severely limited last year, as he averaged a career-low 5.2 rushing attempts and 26.8 rushing yards per game. He had previously averaged at least 51.3 yards per game in every full season as a starter. He's averaging 36.0 yards per game so far this year, but he did leave one of those games at halftime.If Jackson is again unable to start against Cincinnati, Tyler Huntley would once again take his place under center. Huntley has gone 1-1 in his two starts, and he's 51 of 72 for 429 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions so far. He's also run 15 times for 64 yards and a touchdown. The Ravens managed 30 points in their overtime victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, but slumped to just 10 points in their loss to the Cleveland Browns last week. 
The offense has looked electric with Jackson under center in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's scheme, but we have rarely seen it at full strength so far this year. Not only has Jackson missed two-plus games, but Zay Flowers also missed a game-and-a-half and was limited to just 33% of the snaps in another. If they can get fully healthy, the Ravens could take off offensively. But that all depends on Jackson's ankle.

The pair of Englishmen were joined by Branden Grace, Tom McKibbin and Lucas Herbert on Friday as the deadline for player commitment to the league is Oct. 25."Wanted to confirm that I will not be a part of LIV 2.0," Hatton wrote on his Instagram story. "A big thank you to everyone for their continued support. I am excited for what the next chapter of my career holds. Looking forward to seeing you all in Abu Dhabi."Hatton has eyes on the DP World Tour playoffs, which begin in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 5-8, where he will make his first start since departing from LIV Golf. He will be joined in the field by his Legion XIII teammate and captain, Jon Rahm, who had already made it known that he wants nothing to do with the league moving forward.Rahm's lawyer stated that his client found the terms for LIV Golf 2.0 "unacceptable" before the two parties reached a separation agreement in which the Spaniard retained his name, image and likeness rights. Like Rahm, Hatton has playing privileges on the DP World Tour thanks to his previous victories on the circuit.The same will go for Poulter and the rest of the lot who can return to the DP World Tour in November. In his statement, the 12-time DP World Tour winner cited wanting to spend more time with his family, grow his YouTube channel and compete in some senior events as reasons for leaving LIV Golf and the Majesticks, which he has captained since the start.
"Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career," Poulter released in a statement.The DP World Tour put its foot in the ground two weeks ago when the league announced that any player who played in LIV Golf 2.0 would not be able to take up membership on the European circuit in 2027. To be eligible for the European Ryder Cup team, one must be a member of the DP World Tour.Other players who have indicated that they will no longer be playing on LIV Golf include Adrian Meronk, Louis Oosthuizen, Sergio Garcia, Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell III, Thomas Pieters and David Puig. Meanwhile, those who plan to play in the league should it get off the ground include Richard Bland, Ben Campbell, Cameron Tringale and Brendan Steele.
"This is where I want to be," Steele recently said. "This has been home to me for the last four years, it's been great. I'm happy to stay."

Walter has been shedding assets amid an FBI and SEC investigation into his wealth management firm

        Embattled Los Angeles Sparks owner Mark Walter is looking to sell the franchise and its yet-unopened practice facility for $700 million, according to Bloomberg. Walter bought the Sparks, one of the WNBA's original franchises, for around $10 million in 2014. If Walter is able to get $700 million for the Sparks, that would smash the record for the most expensive franchise sale in WNBA history, even if you subtract the cost of the practice facility, which was built for $150 million and is expected to open in 2027. Notably, Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, who bought the Los Angeles Lakers from Walter earlier this year, are reportedly not interested in the Sparks. The current record for the most expensive franchise sale was set earlier this year when Tilman Fertitta bought the Connecticut Sun for $300 million with a plan to move the franchise to Houston and revive the Comets in 2027. Sparks have already undergone massive changes this yearThe Sparks went an extremely disappointing 16-28 this season and missed the playoffs for the sixth consecutive season. That is not only the longest active playoff drought in franchise history, but the longest active one in the league. Yet another failure led to massive changes across the board.
Stacy Johns, the previous CEO of Bay FC in the NWSL, was hired as the team's new president in April, just days before the season started.General manager Raegan Pebley was fired in July and later replaced by Ariana Andonian, the former general manager of the Philadelphia 76ers' G League affiliate.Coach Lynne Roberts was fired immediately after the season ended. She went 37-51 in her two seasons in charge. The organization has not yet hired a replacement.Star guard Kelsey Plum was traded ahead of the deadline for Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.Star forward Nneka Ogwumike announced her retirement.Now, Johns and Andonian will brace for an ownership change as they try to reshape the Sparks' coaching staff and roster. 
        
            
                Sparks fire Lynne Roberts: Los Angeles moves on from second-year coach as team's postseason drought continues
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Walter selling off sports teams amid investigationsEarlier this year, Walter sold the Lakers to Kushner and Iger for a record-setting $12.5 billion barely a year after buying them for $10 billion. He has since sold his stake in Chelsea FC to Clearlake Capital, but has insisted that the Los Angeles Dodgers are not for sale. Walter also owns the entire PWHL (Professional Women's Hockey League) and the Cadillac F1 team. Walter is also the CEO of Guggenheim Partners, an investment and wealth management firm based in New York City. Last year, "federal prosecutors in Manhattan began examining Guggenheim's $362 billion money management arm," Bloomberg reported in July. Regulators are reportedly investigating whether Walter and Guggenheim properly disclosed billions of dollars of loans.
The FBI and Securities and Exchange Commission are collaborating on the investigation, which also involves two of Walter's insurance companies, Delaware Life Insurance Co. and Clear Spring Life and Annuity Co. The investigation was opened due to an internal whistleblower complaint, per the Wall Street Journal. Here's more from the WSJ:"The U.S. Attorney's Office in Manhattan and the Securities and Exchange Commission are now examining how around $16 billion in loans extended to companies tied to Walter or his conglomerate, TWG Global, wound up on the books of insurance companies he owns after passing through a third entity, the people familiar with the matter said. The authorities are trying to determine whether the activity constituted fraud, one of the people said."Such related-party transactions must be disclosed to insurance regulators, a rule meant to limit conflicts of interest and protect policyholders. Walter's insurance firms said in recent filings that they had reviewed their transactions after receiving subpoenas and had identified problems with how certain transactions were presented."In a statement to the WSJ, a TWG spokesperson said that, "Mark Walter and TWG have always acted in good faith, and those who have done business with Mark know him as honest and straightforward. Nothing about these transactions was any different."Meanwhile, TWG has been trying to raise cash to help pay down some of those loans, Bloomberg reported in August, describing them as "aggressive efforts to reduce the affiliated loans on the balance sheet of its insurers or to restructure some of them."

As Drake Maye's numbers have gotten hot, so too have Hunter Henry's. In the past three weeks Henry has turned 14 targets into a 12-154-2 stat line and more importantly 11-plus PPR points per game. He's become a go-to in the red zone for Maye, getting first reads and leading the team with four targets near the paint. He especially seemed to be on the same page as Maye on their touchdown last week. Henry has also become a short-area outlet when Maye's been pressured and/or needs to check the ball down -- six of his 14 targets have come in those specific situations since Week 4. While it means there aren't a lot of plays designed for Henry, it's still two good roles for an older, slower tight end, especially on a short week versus a depleted defense. Chicago has allowed an 86% catch rate to tight ends in the red zone this year with Kyle Pitts cashing in twice on them last week. Henry is a low-end starter.  Caleb Williams had two 2-yard runs, had a season low 3.23-second time to throw rate and a season low with Ben Johnson, 3.9-yard average depth of throw against the Falcons last week. That tells me he's still not 100% recovered from his hamstring injury, but it didn't quite turn him into a game manager. Five of his six biggest gains involved him holding the ball for at least three seconds, be it because he moved out of the pocket or not, and that doesn't include his 14-yard touchdown to Colston Loveland, where he escaped pressure and did the whole hold-and-throw-cross-body thing that he seems to live and die by. Williams is dangerous if he's mobile, but his Fantasy upside is lowered if he won't run downfield. The Patriots pass rush has been inconsistent all year but they tend to rack up sacks against statue QBs. Even with a couple of question marks along his O-line, Williams should be able to overcome their pressure and hit targets downfield. Last week, he completed all 26 of his throws for 255 yards when he wasn't pressured. That's bad news for the Patriots and good news for Williams. Luther Burden III had a great stat line last week -- 8-95-0 on eight targets -- but he didn't start, and he played just 39% of the snaps and ran a route on just 44% of Williams' dropbacks, both season lows. This happened because the Bears played with two or more tight ends on 67% of their plays, their second-highest mark of the season. Burden played just five snaps with Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet -- and had his biggest play of the day on one of them! There are only two ranked games featuring top-25 teams in Week 8, and each involves a Texas school.No. 7 Ole Miss travels to No. 19 Texas (7:30 p.m. ET) in what feels like a referendum game for both Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian and starting quarterback Arch Manning. The narratives have gone into overdrive this week as Texas has lost its last two games, both to unranked opponents, as the Manning-led Texas offense has struggled mightily. To get back on track, Arch will have to beat the program that means so much to his family. Arch's father (Cooper), uncle (Eli) and grandfather (Archie) all played football at Ole Miss. Later in the night, No. 14 Houston takes on No. 10 Utah in a game that has both Big 12 championship and College Football Playoff implications. The Utes didn't look great in a win against Colorado last week but remain one of the five last unbeaten Power Four teams. Houston's lone loss is a two-point defeat to Texas Tech, and the Cougars could take a big step toward being a CFP contender with a road win over Utah. Other intriguing games include No. 6 Indiana at Michigan, No. 18 LSU at Auburn and No. 11 Tennessee at South Carolina. The Hoosiers are coming off a tough loss to Ohio State, while the Wolverines may have found something with true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr. In the battle of the Tigers, LSU will need a win to keep its playoff hopes alive. Tennessee catapulted itself up the SEC hierarchy with a win over Alabama last weekend and yet still is a 2.5-point underdog to the Gamecocks.
After a historic weekend that saw five top eight-ranked teams go down on a single day, the Week 8 slate isn't quite as promising, but there's plenty to get excited about.  Michigan vs. No. 6 Indiana 12 p.m. on Fox, Fubo (try free): We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP, and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. body:
A midseason All-American with 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, the breakout freshman delivers a massive statement for the Beavers by bypassing the transfer portal
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jesse Legree – the nation's most exciting freshman and a midseason CBS Sports All-America selection – announced to the world Friday from his home gym in Baltimore, Maryland, that he will be returning to Oregon State for his sophomore season. Legree made the announcement and re-signed with the Beavers live on CBS Sports HQ. Legree's intent during the bye week was to put to rest doubts about his future and quiet portal whispers that had already begun as scouting departments around the country, beginning to devise their 2027 roster-building plans, took full notice of the 5-foot-9 Legree's exploits in Corvallis: 46 receptions and a nation-leading 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. "I, here, will be signing to Oregon State Beavers for the 2027 to 2028 season," Legree said. "It's always some kids' dream to live out on signing day, and unfortunately, I wasn't able to have mine last year. And to be able to have one this year for this contract is great."The signing day Legree never truly hadLast December, he watched his teammates at St. Frances Academy in Baltimore sign with the likes of Alabama and Auburn. Legree was an unheralded three-star prospect with few high-level offers and no signing day home, at least during the school's morning celebrations. Legree grew up a basketball player and played defensive back his first three years of high school football. 
He joked with CBS Sports in early October that he "barely knew Oregon was a state." But newly minted Beavers general manager Eron Hodges had seen Legree while he and new OSU coach JaMarcus Shephard were at Alabama during the 2025 season, the byproduct of scouting and recruiting Bama signee Jireh Edwards, a teammate of Legree's at St. Frances Academy. "The day I got the job, Eron called me and said, 'Hey, watch this kid right now.' And I watched him right away, knowing that Eron was gonna come out here and be the GM with me," Shephard said. "And I was like, 'Yeah, we need to go get him. Let's get him.' And we started that process the day that I got the job, and so he was the first kid that I watched as the head football coach here at Oregon State, and he was the first person that I knew for sure we wanted on our team."Now, if I'm just being transparent, I didn't know for sure how good of a receiver he was. You know, his highlight tape has him doing a lot of returns. But I also watched some of his basketball stuff. You can see his quickness, change of direction, explosiveness, ability to track the ball, and all that stuff. And you're really just hoping that all that would translate into a receiver."
Oregon State called late in the day on the opening day of Early Signing Period, long after his teammates had signed and had their moment. His high school coach, Messay Hailemariam, received a text from Hodges that said, "he has a home with us if he wants it. We want to take him."Hailemariam remembers interrupting his team during a film session to share the news. 
This decision is about loyalty Legree has won seven straight Pac-12 Freshman of the Week awards. The only reason he won't win an eighth is that the Beavers are on a bye in Week 8. Legree leads the nation in yards (1,040) and touchdowns (14) and has been the catalyst for a prolific OSU offense that's sixth nationally in yards/play (7.32) and fifth in yards per game (527) and fourth in scoring offense (42.7 points per game). The Beavers are 5-2 and rolling as they get into the toughest part of their Pac-12 schedule (transfer QB Braden Atkinson, who will also have a decision to make about his 2027 future, has been great).
In today's college football, the moment a player at the Group of Six level begins to shine, there is an assumption that he will move on to what people assume are greener pastures. Conventional wisdom doubts that Oregon State can do what's necessary to keep him, but Legree is not a conventional player, and his relationship with Oregon State is not the conventional business transaction that is the new order of the day in college football. They took a chance on him, and he rewarded it at the commitment ceremony he never had. For Oregon State, this is a statement of intent as well. College football forgot about Corvallis. Its own in-state rival left them for the Big Ten, and the Beavers were left to pick up the pieces of the Pac-12 with Washington State. They're rising from the ashes to build something exciting, and retaining Jesee Legree is a big boost to the project.

        Davante Adams (hamstring) is already out for Week 7 at Las Vegas, and now Puka Nacua (calf) might not play. That's bad news for Matthew Stafford, but someone is going to have to step up and make plays in the passing game. With that in mind, we're looking at Konata Mumpfield and Tyler Higbee as sleepers.  Now, as of Friday afternoon, Nacua has not been ruled out yet. He will work out before Sunday's game, and hopefully he'll be able to play against the Raiders. But leaving practice Thursday and not being able to practice Friday is a bad sign.  I would rank Stafford's pass catchers without Nacua and Adams as Higbee, Mumpfield, Colby Parkinson, Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington and Davis Allen. But Higbee and Mumpfield are the only two worth using in most Fantasy leagues.  Higbee comes into Week 7 having scored at least 11.7 PPR points in three of his past four games. He was great in Week 3 at Denver when Nacua was sidelined with a groin injury, with eight catches for 62 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets.  This is a great matchup against the Raiders, who are No. 7 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing tight ends. Six tight ends have scored at least 10.7 PPR points against Las Vegas this year, including twice in the same game with Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant in Week 3 and Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon in Week 5.  That bodes well for Higbee and Parkinson, who just had 14.1 PPR points in Week 6 against Arizona. I like Parkinson as an option in deeper leagues, but Higbee should be considered a borderline No. 1 tight end in all formats.  Mumpfield was already in play as a sleeper with Adams on injured reserve. In Week 3, without Nacua, Mumpfield had four catches for 93 yards and a touchdown on eight targets.  We'll see how Stafford and Sean McVay use Mumpfield, Whittington and Atwell, but Mumpfield has the most upside going into Week 7. He has 13 targets this season, while Atwell (four) and Whittington (three) have combined for seven.  This matchup is favorable since nine receivers have scored at least 10.9 PPR points against Las Vegas, including seven touchdowns. I view Mumpfield as a borderline starter in three-receiver leagues if Nacua can't play.  Again, Nacua hasn't been ruled out yet. But it's trending in the wrong direction, and Fantasy managers might benefit with Higbee and Mumpfield as sleepers in Week 7.

body:
As we get ready for Sunday's slate, there is no shortage of injury news for the Week 7 games. This week, there are some major potential returns and some key players sidelined.Two of the biggest returns we could see this week involve quarterbacks. Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) is questionable and is looking to make his first appearance since Sept. 27. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is questionable and says he is trending in the right direction to play in the divisional game against the Bengals.Here's a look at game designations for all of Sunday's matchups:Steelers (-3.5) vs. SaintsSteelers: WR Ben Skowronek (calf), CB Brandin Echols (hamstring) OUT; RB Rico Dowdle (knee), S DeShon Elliott (knee) QUESTIONABLESaints: G Cesar Ruiz (knee), DT Nathan Shepherd (illness) QUESTIONABLEThe Steelers and Saints are in France this week, playing at Stade de France just outside of Paris. Steelers S DeShon Elliott (knee) is in his 21-day window to return, and with a full week of full participation in practice, a return feels possible. RB Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited in practice all week. T.J. Watt (calf) showed up on the injury report and increased his workload from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and a full participant Friday. Head coach Mike McCarthy said he wasn't concerned about his star LB's status.Over on the Saints side, just two players are listed on Friday's injury report. G Cesar Ruiz is officially questionable and was able to practice on a limited basis after not participating earlier in the week. If he is unable to play, rookie Jeremiah Wright could be put in his place. DT Nathan Shepherd has missed the last two games. Head coach Kellen Moore would not give details on Shepherd, who didn't practice Friday after practicing all week. RB Alvin Kamara, who was limited all week with a back injury, has no game designation.
49ers (-3.5) vs. Falcons49ers: WR Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf), LB Luke Gifford (groin), LB Garret Wallow (hamstring), S Marques Sigle (ankle) OUT; WR Christian Kirk, CB Upton Stout (shoulder), S Siran Neal (knee) QUESTIONABLEFalcons: RB Brian Robinson (hamstring), OT Michael Jerrell (bicep), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) OUT; WR Beaux Collins (hip), WR Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), OT Cameron Williams (ankle), DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring), DE Za'Darius Smith (neck), DT Gervon Dexter (hamstring), LB Kendal Daniels (neck), CB C.J. Henderson (groin), CB A.J. Terrell (groin), CB Avieon Terrell (back) QUESTIONABLESan Francisco is looking to stay perfect this week, but once again has the weight of significant injuries hindering it. The offense will be without two top wide receivers, with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) both ruled out ahead of the matchup. This is the second straight missed game for Samuel. As expected DE Nick Bosa (knee, calf) is also out. DL Mykel Williams (knee), who was sidelined to start the year, did not have a game designation this week after being upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a full participant on Friday.The Falcons have a lengthy injury report this week, ruling out four players, including RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (forearm). With Deablo out, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable, could get the nod. CB A.J. Terrell (groin) and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) could make their return this week. Terrell spent the last four weeks on IR. Bengals vs. Ravens (-3)Bengals: No injury designations.Ravens: OLB Tavius Robinson (pectoral), S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) OUT; CB T.J. Tampa (knee) DOUBTFUL; QB Lamar Jackson (ankle), DT Broderick Washington (ankle) QUESTIONABLEOnly four Bengals players landed on the injury report this week. The three players who did not practice on Friday, DT Jonathan Allen, DT B.J. Hill and DT Dexter Lawrence, were all listed as "not injury related, rest."
QB Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, says he is trending in the right direction to make his return against the Bengals. He is officially questionable after being limited all week. DT Broderick Washington (ankle) is also questionable and was limited all week. CB T.J. Tampa (knee) was limited all week and is their one doubtful player. Buccaneers vs. Panthers (-3.5)Buccaneers: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) OUT; QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) QUESTIONABLEPanthers: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) OUT; OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) QUESTIONABLEThe biggest takeaway from the Buccaneers injury report is the possibility of a return from starting QB Baker Mayfield, who has been dealing with a right thumb injury. He's missed the last three games, and in his place, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has led the offense. If he does come back, he will be without WR Emeka Egbuka, who currently leads the team in receiving yards (240). On the other side of the ball, S Antoine Winfield will miss his second straight game. Panthers QB Bryce Young (knee) was listed on the injury report, but doesn't get a game designation and was a full participant all week. OT Monroe Freeling (knee) and LB Bam Martin-Scott were full participants all week, but get the questionable stamp.
Giants vs. Texans (-10)Giants: LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder), CB Greg Newsome II (concussion) OUT; TE Theo Johnson (neck) DOUBTFUL; OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), OL Marcus Mbow (knee), CB Paulson Adebo (knee), S Jevon Holland (concussion), S Tyler Nubin (neck) QUESTIONABLE Texans: RB David Montgomery (groin), OT Blake Fisher (thumb), S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand), S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) OUT; WR Tank Dell (knee) QUESTIONABLEGiants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) is reportedly out for the year, but at minimum is sidelined for this week. CB Greg Newsome (concussion) joins him as the only other Giant ruled out ahead of the matchup. TE Theo Johnson is doubtful after not practicing on Friday. S Jevon Holland (concussion) and OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) were limited the last two days after both not participating on Wednesday.The Texans could get WR Tank Dell (knee), who hasn't played since 2024, back this week. He is questionable after being a full participant on Wednesday and Thursday. Among those already ruled out are S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) and RB David Montgomery (groin). Colts vs. Vikings (-6.5)Colts: WR Anthony Gould (concussion), TE Tyler Warren (groin), CB Sauce Gardner (calf) OUT; LB CJ Allen (ankle), LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), CB Justin Walley (knee), P Rigoberto Sanchez (right foot) QUESTIONABLEVikings: RB Jordan Mason (thumb) QUESTIONABLEThe Colts injury report was lengthy this week. CB Sauce Gardner (calf) is out after suffering the injury in last week's loss. He did not practice all week. Tyler Warren (groin), who leads the team in receptions among TEs, is also out. CB Justin Walley (knee) didn't practice Wednesday and was limited the rest of the week. LB CJ Allen (ankle) and LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) were both non-participants on Friday.
Minnesota's injury report is very short this week, with just one player carrying a game designation. RB Jordan Mason (thumb) was a full participant all week. WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited to start the week, but after two full practices, is cleared to play. WR Jordan Addison (hamstring) will make his return after missing one week and getting extra time to rest during last week's bye. TE T.J. Hockenson is another who took full advantage of the rest, passing the concussion protocol and ruled good to go for this week.Dolphins vs. Jets (-4.5)Dolphins: CB Reese Taylor (quad) OUT; EDGE Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring) DOUBTFUL; LB Willie Gay Jr. (illness), S Kyle Louis (knee) QUESTIONABLEJets: OL Max Mitchell (concussion), EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), LB Francisco Mauigoa (quad) OUT; RB Breece Hall (quad), RB Kene Nwangwu (knee), OL Dylan Parham (knee) QUESTIONABLEMiami has one player ruled out ahead of the divisional matchup, as they look to get their first win of the year. LB Willie Gay (illness) is questionable and was limited in practice on Friday. S Kyle Louis (knee) was a full participant on Friday after being limited the rest of the week. Jets RB Breece Hall, who has missed multiple weeks with a quad injury, could return to the offense this week. He was limited in practice over the last two days, an improvement over Wednesday's practice, when he was sidelined. The RB is officially questionable. EDGE Joseph Ossai remains out, missing his third straught game.
Browns (-1.5) vs. TitansBrowns: QB Dillon Gabriel (back), G Teven Jenkins (back), DT Khalil Davis (quad), DT Mike Hall (ankle) OUT; RB Dylan Sampson (knee), LB Quincy Williams (neck), CB Denzel Ward (hand), S Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) QUESTIONABLETitans: RB Tyjae Spears (knee), WR Calvin Ridley (hip), LB Dorian Mausi (foot), S Tony Adams (ankle), S Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) QUESTIONABLEThe Browns have a lengthy injury report this week with three players out, including DT Khalil Davis (quad) and G Teven Jenkins (back). CB Denzel Ward (hand) popped up in the injury report as limited on Friday and officially questionable. S Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) was limited the last two days after not participating on Wednesday.The Titans did not rule out any players ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, and five players are listed as questionable. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) went from limited Wednesday to not practicing the next two days. RB Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited on Friday. Safties Tony Adams (ankle) and Kevin Winston (quad) were both limited the first two days of the week and ended as full participants.Broncos (-4.5) vs. CardinalsBroncos: RB Tyler Badie (thumb), OLB Jonah Elliss (ankle), S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) OUT; RB Jonah Coleman (ankle), CB Patrick Surtain II (ankle) QUESTIONABLECardinals: RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), OL Jon Gaines II (knee/ankle), DL Walter Nolen (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee) OUT; QB Carson Beck (back), DL Darius Robinson (back), CB Max Melton (knee), S Budda Baker (groin/illness) QUESTIONABLEThe Broncos will once again be without S Talanoa Hufanga, who suffered an ankle injury in Week 5. Denver has a few players who could return after missing multiple games. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) is questionable and was limited in practice this week, after missing the last two games. RB Jonah Coleman could make his return from IR and was a full participant all week. 
The Cardinals are dealing with numerous injuries this week. S Budda Baker played through injury in their Week 6 matchup but missed two days of practice before he was upgraded to limited on Friday. Another questionable player is CB Max Melton (knee), who did not practice the last two weeks. RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), who leads the team in rushing, will be out this week. Packers vs. Lions (-3)Packers: LB Zaire Franklin (shin) OUT; WR Bo Melton (back), G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) QUESTIONABLELions: C Cade Mays (wrist), S Brian Branch (Achilles) QUESTIONABLEPackers LB Zaire Franklin is out for only the second time in his nine-year career. Franklin suffered the injury during Thursday's practice. DT Jordon Riley (Achilles) is on the PUP list and could make his return this week, after being limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. QB Jordan Love (back) and WR Christian Watson (ankle) were both on the injury report this week, but carry no game designations. The Lions have a short report this Friday. Just two players, C Cade Mays (wrist) and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are both questionable after full week's of practice. The only other player to land on the injury report this week was CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring), who was a full participant on Friday and doesn't carry a game designation.
Rams (-4.5) vs. RaidersRams: LB Nate Landman (concussion) OUT; WR Puka Nacua (calf), CB Trent McDuffie (groin) QUESTIONABLERaiders: WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. (hamstring), TE Carter Runyon (foot) OUT; RB Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) QUESTIONABLEThe Rams could be without WR Puka Nacua (calf), who already missed two games this week. CB Trent McDuffie (groin), missed last week and is officially questionable, despite not practicing all week. The Rams are struggling at 2-4 and can use all the help they can get as they look to turn their season around. The Raiders ruled two players out, WR Dont'e Thornton (hamstring) and TE Carter Runyon (foot) ahead of Sunday's matchup. The Raiders, who have the fourth-fewest rushing yards by any offense in the league, could be without RB Washington (foot/back), who is questionable. Washington, who has the second-most rushing yards on the team, did not practice the last two days. TE Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) was limited on Wednesday, but was back in full gear the rest of the week. Chiefs vs. Seahawks (-2.5)Chiefs: RB Brashard Smith (hamstring), WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), OL Jaylon Moore (concussion) OUT; LB Cooper McDonald (knee), CB L'Jarius Sneed (knee) QUESTIONABLESeahawks: RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), LB Chazz Surratt (calf), LB Drake Thomas (ankle) OUT; QB Drew Lock (right elbow), LB Demarcus Lawrence (knee), LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip), LB Connor O'Toole (hamstring), S Nick Emmanwori (hip) QUESTIONABLEThe Chiefs offense will be without RB Brashard Smith (hamstring), who was downgraded from limited Thursday to a non-participant on Friday. They will also be without WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) for the second week in a row. CB L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was limited all week and is questionable. TE Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited all week but carries no game designation. QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) was also on the injury report but was at full capacity in practice all week. 
Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip) popped up on the injury report as a limited participant in Friday's practice and carries a questionable status. QB Drew Lock (right elbow), LB Demarcus Lawrence (knee), LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip), LB Connor O'Toole (hamstring) were all also limited on Friday and are questionable.
